shots.action: Night meadow. Camera cranes down from a sky full of stars into tall grass; one faint glow among the blades.
shots.caption: Once, a small firefly looked up at the stars.

shots.action: Close-up: the firefly sits on a blade tip looking up, its light pulsing weakly.
shots.caption: They were so bright. And it was so small.

shots.action: It takes off and climbs; the grass falls away, the sky fills the frame.
shots.caption: So it flew up to join them.

shots.action: High above the meadow, a tiny light against a huge sky and moon. It slows, wavers; its light flickers low.
shots.caption: But however high it climbed, the stars came no closer.

shots.action: It sinks like a dim ember back down into the dark grass.
Ground level, deep grass like a forest. A tiny mouse, lost, shivering. Almost no light. A faint glow drifts in from above.
shots.caption: Down in the tall grass, a mouse had lost its way home.

shots.action: Two-shot. The firefly hovers before the mouse and brightens; warm light spreads over the mouse's face and through the blades.
shots.caption: The firefly had only a little light.

shots.action: Side tracking shot: the firefly leads, the mouse hops behind through the grass and past red mushrooms; blade shadows sweep.
shots.caption: But a little light, close by, goes a long way.

shots.action: Crossing a still pond on a fallen twig; the firefly and the stars mirrored in the water.
A mushroom house with a warm lit window. The mouse reaches the door and turns to look back up.
Camera rises and pulls back over the meadow; the firefly hovers above the roof, one bright point beneath the stars. Hold for the moral.
shots.caption: From its doorway, the mouse looked up, and saw the brightest star in the sky.
shots.moral: You don't have to reach the stars to be one.

shots.action: Making-of breakdown: raw geometry, one sample of noise, converged light.

narration.note: The narration is the one part of the film that is not code: an AI voice reads the captions.

lines.text: Once, a small firefly looked up at the stars.
They were so bright. And it was so small.
So it flew up to join them.
But however high it climbed, the stars came no closer.
Down in the tall grass, a mouse had lost its way home.
The firefly had only a little light.
But a little light, close by, goes a long way.
From its doorway, the mouse looked up, and saw the brightest star in the sky.
You don't have to reach the stars to be one.
Every shape, every ray of light and every note in this film was written as code, by Claude Fable 5.2.
